newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB sells Brazil up to 600,000 T wheat at US$150.
newsitem.headline: CWB sells Brazil up to 600,000 T wheat at US$150.

text.p: The Canadian Wheat Board overnight sold to Brazil up to 600,000 tonnes of milling wheat at US$150/tonne FOB St. Lawrence for May-July delivery, grain trade sources said.
"I've heard they sold them 600,000 tonnes. The price is US$150 to US$155 (a tonne) FOB St. Lawrence. It's for May, June, July," one source said.
Brazil's largest milling group J. Nacedo and a Bunge milling subsidiary were the buyers of the Canadian wheat to be blended, two sources said.
CWB officials were not immediately available for comment.

"They probably sold it out of St. Lawrence around US$150, US$151 (a tonne) which would be about US$190 CIF, tax paid in Brazil. That's what you look at. Argentine wheat's at US$168 in the last prices, lets say US$163," a source said.
Freight from the St. Lawrence River is about US$17/tonne and a 10 percent tax is levied on wheat shipped into Brazil, the source said.
